chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is obligatory for the believer upon the believer to offer sincere advice to him, in his presence and in his absence.
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of a believer towards another believer regarding advice?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish 'al-nasiha' as a binding right (haqq) of the believer upon the believer, extending beyond mere recommendation to an obligatory duty. The distinction between 'al-mashhad' (presence) and 'al-maghieb'' (absence) underscores the comprehensive nature of this bond, ensuring sincerity is not limited to public discourse but includes private counsel and behind-the-back support. This concept is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding social cohesion and the spiritual accountability of the community.
